videos.script: Lesson 13 said a constructor builds an object. That is most of the truth, and this lesson is the rest. {{blocks}} A class can carry code outside every method: a static block, run once for the class, and an instance block, run for every object. {{order}} Then one program that prints each step as it happens. Seven numbered lines, for a class and the class it extends. Two of them happen only once, however many objects you make. The other five happen every time. {{trap}} Last, the trap the order sets. A constructor that calls a method the subclass overrides sees fields that are not set yet. A final field reads null. A field set to a hundred reads zero. {{fix}} Java 25 lets a constructor run code before it calls super, and that closes half of the trap. By the end you can say, for any line in a class, when it runs.
